findings.statement: CA9 protein is up in tumour vs normal (log2FC 2.269, padj 9.9e-43), with a much larger RNA rise; it is a HIF/VHL-loss readout and sits at the top of the convergence ranking, with girentuximab as a clinical-stage antibody.
NNMT protein is strongly up in tumours (log2FC 2.709, padj 1.23e-43); RNA is up in the same direction, it is purity-robust and ranks first-tier in the biomarker profile.
CD70 membrane protein is up in tumours (log2FC 2.421, padj 1.94e-38), concordant with RNA; it has anti-CD70 agents in clinical development, making it an antibody or cell-therapy target candidate.
ENPP3 protein is up in tumours (log2FC 1.544, padj 3.02e-37), concordant with RNA; it is a membrane enzyme with an antibody-drug conjugate (AGS-16C3F) reaching phase 2.

SCARB1 (HDL receptor) protein is up in tumours (log2FC 1.837, padj 5.08e-37) and tops the target profile ranking; membrane-localised, with no DepMap dependency signal so it is a tractability-driven rather than essentiality-driven candidate.

SLC16A3 (MCT4 lactate exporter) protein is up in tumours (log2FC 2.279, padj 5.43e-47), consistent with a glycolytic, HIF-driven phenotype; it is a membrane transporter and sits near the top of the target profile.
SLC2A1 (GLUT1) protein is up in tumours (log2FC 2.051, padj 8.39e-40), supporting the Warburg/HIF-driven glucose uptake program in ccRCC; it is better read as mechanism than as a selective target.

PSAT1 protein is down in tumours (log2FC -1.963, padj 1.77e-33), and it ranks first in the biomarker profile; the loss of this serine pathway enzyme is a tumour-vs-normal discriminator rather than a target.
ALDH6A1 protein is down in tumours (log2FC -1.925, padj 6.24e-40); it reflects loss of proximal tubule metabolic identity and is a biomarker candidate, with frequent copy-number loss in the CNV data.
PCK1 protein is down in tumours (log2FC -1.859, padj 1.08e-32), with a larger RNA decrease; loss of gluconeogenic identity makes it a tissue biomarker, not a target.

caveats: Findings quote protein-layer values only; RNA, phospho, TCGA replication, purity and survival values were taken from the ranking and not cited numerically.
DepMap shows no selective ccRCC dependency for the top up-regulated candidates, so target status rests on expression and tractability, not essentiality.
Fewer than 11 findings were written; mutation recurrence, cis copy number and kinase activity were not queried per gene within the budget.
Bulk tumour vs normal comparisons can be influenced by cell composition; purity extrapolation was only read from the ranking rows.
